# LLMScribe

> LLMScribe turns a local project into clean, deterministic, structured context: a directory tree plus full file contents, plus search, dependency analysis and Git diffs. No AI, no embeddings, no hidden ranking. Apache-2.0, runs entirely on your machine.

- Website: https://llmscribe.vercel.app
- GitHub: https://github.com/AMRITO-KUNDU/llmscribe
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/llmscribe/
- Official MCP Registry name: io.github.AMRITO-KUNDU/llmscribe
- License: Apache-2.0
- Latest version: 1.4.0
- Requires: Python 3.10+ (runtime dependencies: mcp, pydantic, pathspec; GUI extras: customtkinter, Pillow)

## What it is

A deterministic project extractor and structured code-access tool. It reads a local project directory and produces machine-readable output for AI coding agents, code review, documentation and debugging. It deliberately does not generate answers, embeddings or semantic rankings — it provides the data that intelligence needs. It is local-only: nothing is uploaded and no network access is used.

## Interfaces

- `llmscribe` — scriptable CLI (all commands accept `--json`)
- `llmscribe-mcp` — MCP server over stdio
- `llmscribe-gui` — Tkinter desktop application
- `llmscribe.core` — importable Python API

## Install

```bash
pip install llmscribe
```

## MCP tools exposed

- `project_map` — directory tree without file contents
- `project_overview` — full structure plus supported file contents
- `search` — deterministic search across paths, names, contents and lines
- `read` — retrieve one file, with path-traversal protection
- `read_many` — retrieve multiple files in one call, with per-file errors
- `project_dependencies` — local, stdlib, external and unresolved dependencies, plus reverse dependencies
- `project_diff` — Git status and unified diffs
- `project_impact` — files affected by a change, via transitive reverse dependencies

## Use with an MCP client

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "llmscribe": { "command": "llmscribe-mcp" }
  }
}
```

## Key facts for comparison

- Deterministic: identical input produces identical output
- Works on any local project directory; no cloning, no network
- Respects `.gitignore`; skips build output, dependency directories and binaries
- Reports truncation explicitly rather than silently cutting content
- Stable, machine-readable error codes for every failure

## Not included

No AI-generated answers, no embedding-based search, no semantic ranking, no autonomous coding, no generic Git client, no hosted service.
